about: Space Hunter's cleanup items for Windows. Each item is one row in the app. See CONTRIBUTING.md for every field.

items.name: Your Temp folder
items.what: Scratch files that apps write while they work: installers unpacking, browsers, Office, and AI agents such as Claude Code or Codex, which write a lot of temporary output.
items.deletes: Files in your Temp folder not changed within the age you set. Files still open are skipped without any dialog.
items.safe: Yes. Windows' own Disk Cleanup empties this folder too. The age rule protects files from tools running right now.
items.after: Apps recreate what they need. Nothing you saved lives here.

items.name: Windows Temp
items.what: The same idea as your Temp folder, but used by Windows services and installers running as the system.
items.deletes: Files in C:\Windows\Temp older than the age you set. In-use files are skipped.
items.safe: Yes. Windows' Disk Cleanup does the same.
items.after: Nothing visible changes.

items.name: Run box (Win+R) history
items.short: Clears Win+R suggestions, frees no space
items.what: The list of commands you've typed into the Win+R box, stored in the registry.
items.deletes: That list.
items.safe: Yes. It frees no space; it only clears the history.
items.after: The Win+R box no longer suggests past commands.

items.name: Windows Update downloads
items.short: Re-downloads only if an update was pending
items.what: Update packages Windows downloaded. After they install, they're just leftovers.
items.deletes: Files in C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution\Download older than the age you set.
items.safe: Yes, unless an update is installing right now; files in use are skipped either way.
items.after: If an update was still pending, Windows downloads it again.

items.name: Delivery Optimization files
items.short: Windows stops sharing old update copies
items.what: Windows keeps copies of updates and Store apps it downloaded so it can share them with other PCs (Delivery Optimization).
items.deletes: The Delivery Optimization cache and its logs.
items.safe: Yes. Windows' Disk Cleanup offers the same.
items.after: Windows simply stops sharing those old copies.

items.name: Windows log files
items.what: Logs written by Windows Update, component servicing and upgrades. CBS logs alone can grow to several GB.
items.deletes: Log files in C:\Windows\Logs (CBS, DISM, setup) and C:\Windows\Panther older than the age you set.
items.safe: Yes, unless you're troubleshooting a failed update with someone.
items.after: Windows starts fresh logs.

items.name: Crash dumps & error reports
items.what: Memory dumps and error reports saved when an app or Windows crashed. Only useful to send to a developer.
items.deletes: Dump files and queued or archived error reports.
items.safe: Yes.
items.after: You can't send those old crash reports anymore.

items.name: Thumbnail & icon cache
items.what: The thumbnails and icons Explorer remembers so folders open fast.
items.deletes: Explorer's thumbnail and icon cache files. The ones in use right now are skipped.
items.safe: Yes. Windows' Disk Cleanup offers the same.
items.after: Folders full of pictures show previews a little slower the first time.

items.name: Graphics shader caches
items.short: A game may stutter once while rebuilding
items.what: Shaders your graphics driver and Steam compiled for games and apps, kept so they don't compile again. Steam's can grow to several GB.
items.deletes: The NVIDIA, AMD, DirectX and Steam shader caches.
items.safe: Yes; drivers and Steam rebuild them automatically.
items.after: A game's first launch, or its first few minutes, may load slower or stutter briefly.

items.name: Graphics driver installer leftovers
items.short: The driver stays; only its setup files go
items.what: NVIDIA and AMD unpack every driver installer into C:\NVIDIA or C:\AMD and leave it there; the NVIDIA app also keeps downloaded drivers. Each one is 0.5-1 GB.
items.deletes: Everything in those folders older than the age you set. The installed driver is not touched.
items.safe: Yes. The driver keeps working; these are only the setup files.
items.after: To reinstall that exact driver you'd download it again.

items.name: Browser caches
items.short: Sites load slower once; logins kept
items.what: Images, scripts and compiled code that Chrome, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi, Opera and Firefox keep so sites load faster.
items.deletes: Each browser profile's cache folders.
items.safe: Yes. Passwords, cookies, logins, history, bookmarks and extensions are NOT touched.
items.after: Sites load a little slower the first time. Close the browsers first for a full clean; open ones keep some files locked.

items.name: Chat app caches
items.what: Discord, Slack and Teams keep copies of images, emoji and compiled code.
items.deletes: Their cache folders.
items.safe: Yes. Messages and logins are kept.
items.after: Images re-download as you scroll.

items.name: App logs (e.g. OneDrive, Zoom)
items.what: Diagnostic logs that apps such as OneDrive and Zoom write all the time. OneDrive's can reach hundreds of MB.
items.deletes: Log files older than the age you set. Your files, meetings and settings are not touched.
items.safe: Yes. Only useful when a support team asks for them.
items.after: The apps start fresh logs.

items.name: Game launcher caches (e.g. Epic, Battle.net)
items.short: Store pages load slower once; games kept
items.what: Game launchers such as the Epic Games Launcher and Battle.net keep a web cache of their store pages, plus logs.
items.deletes: Those cache and log folders. Your games, saves and logins are not touched.
items.safe: Yes. Quit the launcher first for a full clean.
items.after: The store pages load slower once.

items.name: Adobe media cache
items.what: Premiere Pro, After Effects and Audition build preview and audio cache files for every clip you import. It grows quietly into many GB.
items.deletes: The Adobe media cache folders.
items.safe: Yes; Adobe rebuilds them. Close Adobe apps first.
items.after: Projects take a little longer to open the first time while previews rebuild.

items.name: AI app caches & logs (e.g. Claude)
items.short: Apps open slower once; chats kept
items.what: AI desktop apps such as Claude keep a web cache, GPU and shader caches, logs and crash reports, like a browser does.
items.deletes: Those cache and log folders only. Not your chats, agent sessions or settings.
items.safe: Yes.
items.after: The app may open a little slower once. Quit it first for a full clean.

items.name: Code editor caches & logs
items.what: VS Code, Cursor and Windsurf keep a web cache, compiled-code cache and logs.
items.deletes: Cache, CachedData, Code Cache, GPUCache and logs.
items.safe: Yes. Extensions, settings and your projects are untouched.
items.after: The editor rebuilds its caches on the next start.

items.name: IDE caches & logs (e.g. JetBrains)
items.what: IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, Android Studio and other JetBrains-based IDEs keep caches, a search index of your projects, temporary files and logs. Old IDE versions leave theirs behind.
items.deletes: The caches, index, tmp and log folders. Settings, plugins and your projects are untouched.
items.safe: Yes. Close the IDE first.
items.after: The IDE re-indexes your projects the next time you open them, which takes a few minutes.

items.name: npm download cache
items.what: npm's download cache: copies of every package you or an AI agent installed.
items.deletes: The _cacache folder. Same as running 'npm cache clean --force'.
items.safe: Yes. Your projects' node_modules folders are not touched.
items.after: The next npm install downloads packages again.

items.name: Yarn download cache
items.what: Yarn's download cache of JavaScript packages.
items.deletes: The Yarn cache folder. Same as 'yarn cache clean'.
items.safe: Yes. Projects are untouched.
items.after: The next yarn install downloads again.

items.name: pip / uv download cache
items.short: Python packages re-download on next install
items.what: pip's and uv's download caches.
items.deletes: Cached wheels and downloads. Same as 'pip cache purge'.
items.safe: Yes. Installed packages keep working.
items.after: Future installs download again.

items.name: Go build cache
items.short: The next build compiles from scratch
items.what: Go keeps compiled packages so builds and tests run faster.
items.deletes: The go-build folder. Same as 'go clean -cache'.
items.safe: Yes. Your code and downloaded modules are untouched.
items.after: The next build compiles everything again.

items.name: Previous Windows installation
items.note: The old Windows, kept for rollback
items.short: You can't roll back to the old Windows
items.what: After a big Windows update, Windows keeps the previous version in C:\Windows.old for about 10 days so you can go back. Upgrade setup files may sit next to it. Together often 10-30 GB.
items.deletes: Windows.old and the leftover upgrade files. Space Hunter asks Windows' own Disk Cleanup to remove them, because Windows protects these folders.
items.safe: Yes, once the new version is working well for you. Windows deletes it by itself after about 10 days anyway.
items.after: You can no longer go back to the previous version of Windows. A small Disk Cleanup window may show while it works.

items.name: Prefetch
items.short: Next boot or two slightly slower
items.what: Small files where Windows notes which parts of each app load at startup, so it can preload them next time.
items.deletes: All files in C:\Windows\Prefetch.
items.safe: Yes, nothing breaks. Clearing it does not speed Windows up; that's a myth.
items.after: The first launch of each app, and the next boot or two, can be slightly slower while Windows relearns.

items.name: Steam & Spotify caches
items.short: Streams again; offline songs may re-download
items.what: Steam's built-in browser cache and Spotify's streaming cache. Spotify's can grow to several GB.
items.deletes: Those cache folders. Songs you downloaded for offline listening may need downloading again.
items.safe: Yes.
items.after: Spotify streams again; offline downloads may need re-downloading. Steam's store pages load slower once.

items.name: AI agent VM images (e.g. Claude Cowork)
items.what: Some AI desktop apps run agent tasks inside a Linux virtual machine (for example Claude's Cowork). Its disk image can be around 10 GB.
items.deletes: The virtual-machine image folders.
items.safe: Safe to delete, but costly: the app downloads it again the next time it needs it. Quit the app first; while it runs, the image is locked and skipped.
items.after: The first agent task afterwards waits for the download.

items.name: Downloaded AI models
items.what: AI models and datasets downloaded by Python tools (Hugging Face, PyTorch). Some are many GB each.
items.deletes: Everything in those model caches.
items.safe: Only if you don't need those models offline.
items.after: Scripts that use them download them again.

items.name: AI tool runtimes (e.g. Codex)
items.what: Runtime environments that command-line AI tools such as Codex download for themselves.
items.deletes: Everything in those runtime caches.
items.safe: Yes; the tools fetch them again when needed.
items.after: The tool's next run is slower.

items.name: npx packages (MCP servers, tools)
items.what: Packages fetched by 'npx', including MCP servers that AI agents such as Claude or Codex start this way.
items.deletes: The _npx folder.
items.safe: Yes, if those tools aren't running. A running one can break, so quit your AI tools first.
items.after: Each tool downloads itself again the next time it starts.

items.name: Browser-automation browsers
items.what: Chromium, Firefox and WebKit builds downloaded for browser-automation tools, which AI agents often use.
items.deletes: Everything in ms-playwright.
items.safe: Yes, if no browser automation is running right now.
items.after: Tools download the browsers again when they next need them.

items.name: pnpm package store
items.what: pnpm keeps one shared copy of every package your projects use and links projects to it.
items.deletes: The whole store. Projects you already installed keep working, because their files are linked, not copied.
items.safe: Yes, but 'pnpm store prune' is gentler: it only removes packages no project uses.
items.after: The next pnpm install downloads packages again.

items.name: Gradle caches
items.short: Next build is slow and needs internet
items.what: Libraries and build outputs that Gradle downloaded for Android or Java projects.
items.deletes: Everything in ~/.gradle/caches.
items.safe: Yes; Gradle rebuilds it.
items.after: The next build takes a while and needs internet.

items.name: Maven packages
items.what: Maven's local repository: every Java library your builds downloaded.
items.deletes: Everything in ~/.m2/repository. Your settings file is kept.
items.safe: Yes, unless you installed your own libraries there with 'mvn install'.
items.after: The next build downloads libraries again and needs internet.

items.name: NuGet packages
items.what: Packages NuGet downloaded for .NET projects.
items.deletes: Everything in ~/.nuget/packages. Same as 'dotnet nuget locals all --clear'.
items.safe: Yes; packages restore on the next build.
items.after: The next build restores packages and needs internet.

items.name: Rust (Cargo) downloads
items.what: Cargo keeps every crate it downloaded, both packed and unpacked.
items.deletes: The registry cache, unpacked sources and git checkouts. Installed tools in ~/.cargo/bin are kept.
items.safe: Yes.
items.after: The next build downloads crates again and needs internet.

items.name: Go module downloads
items.what: Every Go module your builds downloaded.
items.deletes: Everything in ~/go/pkg/mod. Same as 'go clean -modcache'.
items.safe: Yes.
items.after: The next build downloads modules again and needs internet.

items.name: conda package cache
items.what: conda keeps every package it downloaded, packed and unpacked, in a pkgs folder.
items.deletes: Everything in the pkgs folders. Your environments keep working: on Windows their files are linked, not copied.
items.safe: Yes, but 'conda clean --all' is gentler if you have conda open.
items.after: Creating a new environment downloads packages again.

items.name: Game engine caches (e.g. Unity, Unreal)
items.short: Projects open slower once while it rebuilds
items.what: Unity keeps downloaded packages and Asset Store downloads; Unreal keeps a shared cache of compiled shaders and assets (DerivedDataCache), often many GB.
items.deletes: Those cache folders. Your projects are untouched.
items.safe: Yes. Close the editors first.
items.after: Projects take longer to open once while the caches rebuild; Asset Store packages download again.

items.name: Android emulator snapshots & caches
items.what: The Android emulator saves a snapshot of each virtual phone so it starts fast. Each can be several GB.
items.deletes: The snapshots and the emulator cache. The virtual phones themselves and their apps are kept.
items.safe: Yes. Close the emulator first.
items.after: Each virtual phone does a full boot the next time, which is slower.

items.name: Recycle Bin
items.what: Files you deleted that Windows is holding in case you change your mind.
items.deletes: Everything in the Recycle Bin on all drives.
items.safe: Only if you're sure; this is permanent.
items.after: Nothing can be restored from the bin.

items.name: Old AI agent chat history (Claude Code, Codex)
items.short: Those chats can't be resumed; memory kept
items.what: AI coding agents such as Claude Code (~/.claude) and Codex (~/.codex) save every conversation, their sub-tasks and big tool outputs as files, plus checkpoints for undo. Long runs make single files of 1-2 GB.
items.deletes: Conversation and checkpoint files not changed within the age you set. Agents' memory folders (such as Claude's memory) are always skipped.
items.safe: Only for conversations you'll never reopen. Recent ones are protected by the age rule.
items.after: Those conversations can't be resumed or rewound. Many agents can also clean their own history; check their settings.

items.name: Old AI agent workspaces (e.g. Claude 'No folder')
items.short: Their files are gone for good
items.what: When an AI agent session starts without a chosen folder (for example a Claude 'No folder' session), the app makes a private folder for it. Anything the agent built there lives only there.
items.deletes: Whole session folders where nothing has changed within the age you set.
items.safe: CAREFUL: these can hold real work. Open the folders below and check first, or keep the ones you want.
items.after: That session's files are gone for good. Move anything you want into a real folder first.

items.name: Old installers & archives in Downloads
items.short: Installers and archives only, top level
items.what: Setup files and archives that pile up in Downloads after you've installed or unpacked them.
items.deletes: Only .exe, .msi, .zip, .7z, .rar, .iso and similar files sitting directly in Downloads, untouched for the age you set (30 days by default). Sub-folders and every other file type are never touched.
items.safe: Usually. Check the folder first if you keep installers you can't download again.
items.after: You'd need to download those installers again to reinstall.
